review.material: Selected MIT OCW PDFs read: Lecture 1 pp.1–4, Lecture 3 pp.1–3, Lecture 9 pp.1–2, and Lecture 23 pp.1–3.
review.limitations: The full lecture series, exercises and later ring material were not reviewed. Compact notes contain typographical slips; compare the definitions and fully stated maps rather than isolated rendered equations.

sections.title: What these notes help connect
sections.text: A short route from triangle motions to abstract groups, cosets, quotients and actions. The central theme is turning an intuitive classification into a structure whose operations are actually well-defined.

sections.title: The central checks
sections.text: An equivalence relation partitions a set. Cosets give such a partition, but multiplying classes requires an extra check: choosing different representatives must give the same class. Normality makes the proposed quotient multiplication work.

sections.title: Method of explanation
sections.text: The notes use an intentionally bad example: assigning a height to an eye-color class by selecting a person. Different representatives give different heights. The same danger motivates the algebraic proof for quotient groups.

sections.title: From classes to actions
sections.text: A transitive action identifies its acted-on set with the cosets of one stabilizer. For a finite group, orbit size equals group order divided by stabilizer order. The correspondence explains the count rather than merely fitting examples.

sections.title: A practical reading habit
sections.text: Whenever an operation uses a representative, check independence from that choice. Whenever two transformations seem identical, specify what set they act on. Read compositions rightmost-first in these notes.
